The linearization of the 2D inhomogeneous Euler equations about a monotonic shear flow \((U(y),\bar\rho(y))\) reduces the streamfunction to a distorted Rayleigh equation. The critical layer \(U(y)=c\) generates singular generalized eigenfunctions whose Sobolev regularity is sharp at the velocity threshold \(H^{3\pm\tau}\); hence \(s_v=3\). The density perturbation is slaved to the streamfunction by \(\rho'\sim \bar\rho'(y)\psi/(U-c)\), which costs exactly one derivative relative to the velocity field, giving \(s_\rho=2\). Therefore \(s_v+s_\rho=3+2=5\).

Thus $s_\rho=s_v-1=1/2$.  

Hence $s_v+s_\rho=\frac32+\frac12=2$.
